new_cases.place: Fields near Colville's Grove, Rougham / Bradfield St George, Suffolk

new_cases.title: St Chad's Church, Rochdale – the Goblin Builders
new_cases.place: St Chad's Church, Sparrow Hill, Rochdale, Greater Manchester (historic Lancashire)
new_cases.desc: Lancashire legend holds that when the Saxon thane Gamel began a chapel to St Chad by the River Roach, unseen goblin builders repeatedly carried the stones and timber overnight up the hill across the river, where the church was finally built and reached by 124 steps. Versions add a mute boy who vanished while watching the site and returned as a changeling.

new_cases.title: UB-85 'sea monster' U-boat
new_cases.place: Off Stranraer / Loch Ryan approaches, North Channel, Dumfries and Galloway
new_cases.desc: According to a tale attributed to Captain Krech, German submarine UB-85 was recharging on the surface at night in April 1918 when a creature with large eyes in a horny skull and glistening teeth rose alongside, damaging the deck so the boat could not dive; official records say it surrendered to HMS Coreopsis on 30 April 1918. A wreck thought to be UB-85 was found off Stranraer by Scottish Power cable engineers in 2016. Coordinates are approximate (off Stranraer).

new_cases.title: Stonehenge
new_cases.desc: The prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain was built in phases from about 3100 to 1600 BC and is aligned on the summer-solstice sunrise and winter-solstice sunset, with bluestones brought from the Preseli Hills in Wales. Neo-druid and pagan solstice gatherings have taken place there since the early 20th century.

new_cases.title: Tower of London ritual protection marks
new_cases.desc: A 2015 survey for Historic Royal Palaces recorded 54 apotropaic marks at the Tower of London, mostly from the mid-16th to 18th centuries, including 'double V' and mesh symbols and deliberate scorch marks, plus 18th-century objects concealed in a chimney. They were interpreted as staff using folk magic to ward off evil.
